tagline: Pioneer sustainable aerospace for a safe and united world
hero_kpi_rationale: The order book is the primary indicator of future growth in aerospace, reflecting structural demand and the competitiveness of programs such as the A320 or A321XLR.
company_description: Airbus designs, manufactures and sells commercial aircraft, helicopters, satellites and defense systems. The Group is a global leader in aeronautics and space, operating in both civil and military markets.

kpis.name: Revenues
kpis.explanation: Total revenue from all business segments and operations.
kpis.description: Revenue increased through sustained commercial aircraft production and strong performance from helicopters and defense divisions.
kpis.signal: Solid growth driven by strong commercial aircraft demand and increased production rates

kpis.name: EBIT Adjusted
kpis.explanation: Operating profit adjusted for exceptional items and one-time effects.
kpis.description: Adjusted operating margin declined due to supply chain pressures and production challenges, partially offsetting revenue growth.
kpis.signal: Margin pressure despite revenue growth due to supply chain costs and inflation impacts

kpis.name: Order Intake
kpis.explanation: Total value of new commercial orders signed during the period.
kpis.description: The significant decrease is primarily attributable to unfavorable comparison with 2023, which included exceptionally large order contracts.
kpis.signal: Decline reflects tough prior-year comparison with exceptional 2023 order value

kpis.name: Order Book Value
kpis.explanation: Total value of undelivered orders at the end of the reporting period.
kpis.description: Order book reached record levels, supported by sustained demand for commercial aircraft and defense programs.
kpis.signal: Record order book provides multi-year revenue visibility and strong growth foundation

kpis.name: Employees
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees across all Group operations worldwide.
kpis.description: Headcount growth reflects increased production requirements, particularly for commercial aircraft programs.
kpis.signal: Workforce expansion supports increased production cadence on key commercial and defense programs

kpis.name: Scope 1 & 2 GHG
kpis.explanation: Direct and energy-related greenhouse gas emissions from Group operations.
kpis.description: Airbus maintained direct and energy-related emissions stable year-over-year despite increased production volumes.
kpis.signal: Emissions held flat despite production growth demonstrates operational efficiency gains

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of €134.94 B in the latest year

kpis.name: Total Debt
kpis.description: Total debt extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total debt of €11.02 B in the latest year

kpis.name: A321XLR Delivery
kpis.explanation: Operational launch of the new long-range A320 family aircraft variant.
kpis.description: First A321XLR delivery in 2024 marks major technological advancement with 30% fuel savings per seat and 4700 nautical mile range.
kpis.signal: Key milestone enabling market expansion with 30% fuel efficiency gain per seat

kpis.name: H225 Orders
kpis.explanation: Number of H225 helicopter orders, primarily from German Federal Police.
kpis.description: H225 secured record order of 44 units from Germany, reinforcing competitive position in heavy helicopter market.
kpis.signal: Record H225 order from German Federal Police strengthens European defense market positioning

kpis.name: DPS
kpis.explanation: Total dividend amount paid per share during the fiscal year.

risks.title: Increased competition in aerospace markets
risks.summary: Airbus faces intense competition, notably from Boeing, as well as from new regional players. This pressure affects margins, delivery timelines and the ability to innovate rapidly, as observed in the commercial aircraft segment.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is repeatedly mentioned in the document, with strong language on competitive pressure, particularly on commercial programs. The trend is upward due to competitors' expansion. The Competition category is strategic for Airbus.

risks.title: Dependence on critical suppliers
risks.summary: Delays or failures from key suppliers, such as Spirit AeroSystems, can directly impact A320 and A350 production. This led to downward revisions of 2024 forecasts.
risks.score_rationale: The text refers to supply chain disruptions affecting commercial aircraft deliveries. The language is concerned, the trend is stable, and the risk is central to Airbus's industrial operations.

risks.title: Regulatory complexity and certification
risks.summary: Airbus's new programs require strict certification by authorities (EASA, FAA). Any delay in these processes can block deliveries, as seen with the phased rollout of the A321XLR.
risks.score_rationale: The document mentions certification challenges, particularly for new programs such as the A321XLR or automated refueling. The language is technical and cautious, the trend is stable.

risks.title: Cybersecurity in aerospace systems
risks.summary: The increasing connectivity of aircraft and satellites exposes Airbus to cyber threats. Systems such as military satellites SATCOMBw or combat platforms must ensure absolute security.
risks.score_rationale: Although not explicitly detailed, the context of defense and advanced connectivity (e.g. A330 MRTT+) implies a high risk. The language is implicit but serious, the trend is upward.

risks.title: Technological innovation and disruption
risks.summary: Airbus must continuously innovate to remain a leader, particularly in alternative propulsion (hydrogen, SAF) and materials (thermoplastics). Failure to innovate could cause it to lose its technological edge.
risks.score_rationale: The document emphasizes innovation (Racer, MFFD, 3D printing), but also the threat from agile new entrants. The language is strategic and visionary, the trend is upward.

risks.title: Environmental regulation and decarbonization
risks.summary: Airbus is subject to increasing emissions regulations. The development of sustainable fuels, hydrogen aircraft and low-carbon technologies is crucial for its future operating license.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is central in the document, with repeated mentions of SAF, EcoPulse, and regulatory pressure. The language is proactive but urgent, the trend is upward.

risks.title: Geopolitical tensions affecting defense
risks.summary: Geopolitical tensions strengthen demand for defense products (Eurofighter, satellites), but also complicate exports and international supply chains.
risks.score_rationale: The document highlights the impact of global conflicts on defense demand. The language is alarming but strategic, the trend is upward.

risks.title: Intellectual property protection
risks.summary: Airbus's innovations, particularly in space 3D printing or composite materials, are strategic. A leak or theft of intellectual property could compromise its competitive advantages.
risks.score_rationale: Although not directly stated, the intensive R&D programs (Clean Sky, 3D printing) imply a high risk of counterfeiting or espionage. Trend is stable, weight is high.

ai_positioning.summary: Airbus explores artificial intelligence in technology demonstrators and R&D, but without aggressive communication of a centralized AI strategy. Focus remains on sustainable propulsion innovation and decarbonization.
evidence: EcoPulse demonstrator results integrating high-voltage battery systems
ECLIF3 program testing sustainable aviation fuels (SAF)
No mention of generative AI or centralized AI API initiatives in annual reports
